title: Anthropic Investor Briefing Reportedly Omitted ARR Outlook, Contradicting $110B Target Report
summary:
Anthropic did not discuss a September quarter or full year annual revenue run rate outlook during its pre-IPO institutional investor presentation on Wednesday, according to a source familiar with the matter cited by CNBC's Tae Kim, contradicting a Reuters report that the company projected a $110 billion year end run rate at the event. Without official run rate guidance, analysts calculated that Anthropic's $16.8 billion in third quarter revenue implies a September ARR of roughly $70 billion to $74 billion, up from $65 billion at the end of July and below the $76.8 billion estimated by TickerTrends.

During the San Francisco briefing, Anthropic disclosed that third quarter revenue rose about 45% from $11.5 billion to $11.6 billion in the second quarter, slowing from roughly 145% sequential growth in the prior period after first quarter revenue of $4.7 billion. The company posted an 85% adjusted gross margin, an adjusted operating margin above 11%, positive free cash flow and a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit, while outlining plans to spend more than $500 billion on computing and infrastructure over the next decade.

Customers distilling Anthropic's models generated more than $840 million of third quarter revenue before the company banned tens of thousands of distillation accounts. Anthropic plans to begin formally marketing its initial public offering as soon as the week of Nov. 9, though its pre-IPO perpetual contracts on Liquid fell more than 10% over the past month to below a $2 trillion implied valuation, and some investors view $1.5 trillion as more appropriate than the $2 trillion sought by its bankers.

selectedTweets.text:
FT's reported Anthropic Q3 Rev of $16.8B maps out to $74B ARR end of Sept 

Let's use Claude for the math:

- Anchor on July. Anthropic’s run-rate typically annualizes the most recent month, and the last reported mark was $65B at the end of July. Reading that as July revenue × 12 puts July at ~$5.4B.

- Back out August and September: $16.8B − $5.4B = $11.4B. Steady growth of ~3.4% a month fits that, so August is ~$5.6B and September ~$5.8B.

- If $65B was the pace on July 31 rather than July’s revenue, July revenue was lower (~$5.2B, since it was still ramping). That leaves more for August and September and implies ~6.6% a month. September revenue × 12 is still ~$71B, but the pace on Sep 30 is ~$74B.
